id: title:Gilbert09:treat a deleted gcp project as non retryable

review.posthog_relevance: BigQuery warehouse ingestion connector reliability and resource availability handling
review.reason: Adds a terminal classification for GCP project deletion errors in the warehouse ingestion connector, preventing infinite retry loops against deleted resources. P1.F1.H1 adds the error key and message; P1.F2.H1 adds tests. This is a substantive, bounded correctness improvement.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies on supplied observations; no independent verification of actual production incidents or adoption. The tier assumes the connector implementation exists and this entry is used, which is not independently confirmed.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the implementation of the new error key or the updated return value of get_non_retryable_errors, only the addition of the key and a test. The score cannot be assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new entry to the get_non_retryable_errors dictionary, keyed by the string 'has been deleted', with a user-facing error message. This entry is intended to classify a specific GCP project deletion error as terminal rather than retryable.
observations.code_quote: "has been deleted": "BigQuery couldn't complete this sync because the Google Cloud project it uses has been deleted. Restore the project in Google Cloud, or update your source configuration to use a project that still exists, then reconnect the source.",
observations.posthog_connection: This entry allows the BigQuery warehouse ingestion connector to stop retrying a failed sync when the backend GCP project is deleted, preventing an infinite retry loop against a non-existent resource.

observations.behavior: Adds a test case parameterized with two different Forbidden exceptions, both containing the substring 'has been deleted', and asserts that these errors are recognized as non-retryable by the get_non_retryable_errors method.
observations.posthog_connection: This test validates that the connector correctly identifies the specific error message associated with a deleted GCP project, regardless of the HTTP verb or path, and classifies it as a terminal error.
